audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can coset_eval bytes omission allow data substitution while keeping same proof?
audit_items.state_context: The Fiat-Shamir challenge is computed entirely inside c-kzg-4844 C library at eip7594.c:389-478. The Go wrapper is a transparent delegate. No caching of verification results at the cell level.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The Fiat-Shamir challenge hash in c-kzg-4844 v2.1.1 explicitly includes cell bytes (coset evaluations) in the SHA256 input at eip7594.c:457 via memcpy(offset, &cells[i], BYTES_PER_CELL). The Go wrapper is a transparent delegate that passes all parameters unchanged. No state inconsistency is possible at the Go layer for this property.
state_anomalies_found: None — cells are bound in hash
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No caching of KZG verification results occurs for cell-level verification; the batch verifier caches only at the session-batch level (kzgChan draining)
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Concurrent goroutines can submit to kzgChan; all data is immutable RODataColumn after construction so concurrent verification is safe for this property

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The attack requires SHA256 collision to produce same challenge r for different cell bytes. This is computationally infeasible (2^128 security). No concrete counterexample is constructable. Because cells are bound in the hash at eip7594.c:456-458, the challenge r changes when cells change.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: None — cells are hashed; SHA256 collision required to produce same r
attack_scenarios: Theoretically requires SHA256 second-preimage attack — infeasible
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency — verification happens atomically per batch

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The entry point is P2P gossip; attacker controls the cell bytes submitted. However, modifying cells without re-computing the proof would produce a different Fiat-Shamir challenge, making the original proof invalid.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can submit arbitrary cell bytes over P2P, but cells are cryptographically bound in challenge computation

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'cells are bound in Fiat-Shamir challenge' holds. The proof is directly verifiable in eip7594.c:457. The guard is complete — all cells for all batches are included.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient — cells are included in every hash computation, no bypass path exists
edge_cases: Empty cell batch returns ok=true early (line 847-850), but this is caught by ErrNoKzgCommitments in VerifyDataColumnSidecar

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The hypothesis is factually incorrect — coset evaluation bytes are explicitly bound in the Fiat-Shamir hash in the C library at eip7594.c:457. No vulnerability exists for this specific attack vector.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: No fix required. Documentation could clarify that the C library handles all Fiat-Shamir computation per spec.

audit_items.reasoning: The falsification hypothesis is refuted by direct examination of the c-kzg-4844 C library. Cell bytes (coset evaluations) are explicitly included in the SHA256 Fiat-Shamir hash at eip7594.c:457. An attacker modifying cell data will produce a different challenge r, invalidating the original proof. No bypass exists without a SHA256 second-preimage attack.

audit_items.title: Falsification Test: Can proofs[k] omission allow proof substitution between different cells?
audit_items.state_context: The Fiat-Shamir challenge is computed in c-kzg-4844. Proof binding occurs at eip7594.c:460-462 via memcpy(offset, &proofs_bytes[i], BYTES_PER_PROOF).

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Proofs are explicitly included in the Fiat-Shamir hash at eip7594.c:460-462. Each proof is hashed alongside its corresponding cell and commitment index, providing unique binding per (cell, proof) pair. The commitment_indices[i] entry links each proof to its specific commitment.
state_anomalies_found: None — proofs are bound in hash
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No proof-level caching occurs before or after verification
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: No concurrency risk for this property — proofs are immutable 48-byte arrays

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Proof substitution requires either: (a) SHA256 collision on proof bytes, or (b) constructing a valid KZG proof for a different cell that passes the pairing equation. Both are computationally infeasible under standard assumptions (SHA256 second-preimage, KZG soundness).
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: None constructable — proofs are hashed, KZG soundness prevents proof substitution
attack_scenarios: Requires SHA256 second-preimage OR KZG soundness break — both infeasible under standard assumptions

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker can submit arbitrary proof bytes over P2P. Proof bytes are included in both the Fiat-Shamir challenge hash and the pairing equation. Substituting a proof for a different cell produces a different challenge, breaking the pairing verification.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Attacker can submit proofs, but substitution is blocked by both hash binding and pairing check

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'proofs are bound in Fiat-Shamir challenge' holds. The proof binding is at eip7594.c:460-462. The binding is correct and complete.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient — proofs are hashed per cell, no bypass exists
edge_cases: Zero-length proof array: caught by ErrBadArgs in Go binding when lengths don't match

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The hypothesis is factually incorrect — proof bytes are explicitly bound in the Fiat-Shamir hash in eip7594.c:460-462. Proof substitution is prevented by both the hash binding and KZG soundness.

audit_items.reasoning: The falsification hypothesis is refuted by direct examination of eip7594.c:460-462. Proof bytes are included in the SHA256 Fiat-Shamir hash per cell. Substituting Proof_B for Proof_A when verifying Cell_A produces a different challenge r, causing the pairing equation to fail. Additionally, KZG soundness guarantees that no valid proof exists for incorrect evaluation claims, providing a second layer of defense.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does P2P gossip validation invoke batch verification with all parameters correctly passed?
audit_items.state_context: seenDataColumnCache is checked AFTER successful KZG verification. RODataColumn is immutable after construction. SidecarInclusionProven check binds commitments to beacon block header before KZG verification.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: All parameters are passed correctly through the chain. commitments[i] = sidecar.KzgCommitments[i] (per-blob commitment), indices[i] = sidecar.Index (column index, same for all blobs in the sidecar — correct per spec), cells[i] = sidecar.Column[i] (per-blob cell data), proofs[i] = sidecar.KzgProofs[i] (per-blob proof). No truncation, reordering, or transformation occurs. The inclusion proof check (SidecarInclusionProven) precedes KZG verification and binds commitments to the beacon block body root.
state_anomalies_found: Batch timeout returns ValidationIgnore — liveness concern but not soundness bypass
Batching multiple sidecars shares error via resChan; fallback individual verification handles invalid batches correctly
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache is checked after successful KZG verification (not before), preventing cache-based bypass. Cache key is (slot, proposerIndex, columnIndex).
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: kzgChan buffer capacity 100 prevents head-of-line blocking. verifyKzgBatch is called from single kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine, preventing concurrent batch modification.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No parameter corruption path exists. RODataColumn is immutable after blocks.NewRODataColumn() construction. Data is extracted directly from immutable struct fields. No transformation occurs that could corrupt or reorder parameters. The fallback validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg correctly handles individual verification when batch fails.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: None — parameters flow directly from immutable struct fields without transformation
attack_scenarios: Timeout poisoning via kzgChan starvation — causes ValidationIgnore (liveness/DoS, not soundness)
Batch poisoning with invalid sidecar alongside valid sidecar — fallback individual verification prevents harm to valid sidecar
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: Timeout at SecondsPerSlot duration could cause ValidationIgnore for valid sidecars under congestion — DoS risk

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker can send malformed sidecars that flood kzgChan. Malformed sidecars that fail KZG verification are rejected after individual fallback. The only viable attack is DoS via channel saturation causing ValidationIgnore for legitimate sidecars — liveness concern only.
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: kzgChan saturation causing timeout-based ValidationIgnore for legitimate sidecars

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'all parameters are correctly passed to batch verification' holds. Parameter extraction from RODataColumn is direct field access with no transformation. Commitment binding to beacon block header via SidecarInclusionProven prevents commitment substitution attacks.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Immutable RODataColumn type + SidecarInclusionProven check + direct field extraction in VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for parameter correctness. DoS via kzgChan saturation is a separate availability concern.
edge_cases: kzgChan buffer full (100): sendBlocks indefinitely until context cancellation — potential goroutine accumulation under extreme DoS
Context already cancelled: select immediately picks ctx.Done case, returns ValidationIgnore

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Parameter passing is correct and complete. The inclusion proof check binds commitments to the beacon block before KZG verification, preventing parameter substitution. The timeout-based DoS via kzgChan saturation is a known availability trade-off within reasonable bounds (SecondsPerSlot). No soundness vulnerability exists.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Consider monitoring kzgChan queue depth as a health metric. Add kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine supervision/restart logic.

audit_items.reasoning: Parameter passing through the P2P gossip KZG validation chain is correct and complete. The RODataColumn immutability and SidecarInclusionProven check provide strong guards against parameter manipulation. A liveness concern exists via kzgChan saturation DoS, but this does not constitute a soundness (security) vulnerability. The fallback individual verification prevents batch poisoning attacks.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Do validators verify Fiat-Shamir completeness before attesting to blocks with data columns?
audit_items.state_context: Attestation to blocks is independent from data column KZG verification by PeerDAS design. KZG verification gates sidecar forwarding and storage, not block attestation. The SatisfyRequirement call only occurs after ValidationAccept.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The validation flow correctly gates sidecar forwarding on KZG proof verification. SatisfyRequirement(RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified) is only called after ValidationAccept from the batch verifier. TOCTOU analysis shows no window for sidecar modification between verification and storage. Attestation to beacon blocks is independent from data column sidecar KZG verification — this is correct PeerDAS protocol design.
state_anomalies_found: Attestation to blocks does NOT require data column KZG verification — intentional PeerDAS design, not a bug
Timeout (ValidationIgnore) does not satisfy RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified, preventing bypass via timeout
VerifiedRODataColumns() call at line 168 ensures all requirements in GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements are met before sidecar is stored
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache is checked AFTER KZG verification success. Cache key uses (slot, proposerIndex, columnIndex) — prevents replay without re-verification. KZG check precedes cache check.
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: validateDataColumn runs in P2P handler goroutine. kzgVerifierRoutine runs separately. Communication is via channels with no shared mutable state between verification result and msg.ValidatorData assignment.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No TOCTOU window exists between KZG verification and sidecar storage. The batch verifier communicates results via channel and msg.ValidatorData is set atomically after all checks pass. Attestation independence from DAS is a deliberate protocol design choice per the Ethereum Fulu spec.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: None — TOCTOU absent; attestation independence is by design
attack_scenarios: Timeout-based DoS causing ValidationIgnore does not satisfy KZG requirement, preventing bypass
Attestation to block with invalid columns is not exploitable through this code path — attestation is a separate consensus decision
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: kzgChan timeout (SecondsPerSlot) creates window for valid sidecars to be ignored under load — liveness concern only

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attackers can submit sidecars to be processed but cannot bypass KZG verification for storage. The attestation decision is made by separate consensus logic independent of data column sidecar validation results.
entry_points: Consensus attestation (separate, no dependency on KZG sidecar verification)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: Sidecar validation bounded by gossip pipeline. Attestation integrity protected by proposer signature verification and fork choice rules.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'KZG proof verification must succeed before a sidecar is forwarded and stored' holds. SatisfyRequirement is called only on ValidationAccept. VerifiedRODataColumns checks all requirements. The attestation-vs-DAS independence is a spec-level design choice, not an implementation gap.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SatisfyRequirement + VerifiedRODataColumns requirement checker + msg.ValidatorData gating on successful verification
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient for the stated invariant. Attestation independence is intentional protocol design.
edge_cases: If kzgVerifierRoutine crashes, kzgChan blocks indefinitely — goroutine supervision should be verified
Context cancellation after kzgChan send but before resChan receive: handled by ctx.Done case returning ValidationIgnore

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No vulnerability exists. TOCTOU is absent from the implementation. KZG requirement is only satisfied after explicit ValidationAccept. Attestation independence from data column verification is correct Fulu/PeerDAS protocol behavior.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Add goroutine supervision/restart logic for kzgVerifierRoutine to prevent permanent blocking if the goroutine panics or exits unexpectedly.

audit_items.reasoning: The KZG proof verification correctly gates sidecar storage — no bypass exists via timeout (ValidationIgnore) or batch error (fallback to individual). TOCTOU is not present because msg.ValidatorData is set atomically after all requirements are satisfied. Attestation independence from DAS is a PeerDAS protocol design feature, not a vulnerability. Minor operational risk noted: kzgVerifierRoutine goroutine should have supervision to prevent permanent kzgChan blocking on panic.

audit_items.title: Verify Canonical Ordering: Is the hash input order deterministic and consistent across implementations?
audit_items.state_context: The c-kzg-4844 library computes challenge in canonical spec-compliant order within each verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch call. Deduplication of commitments is first-seen order. Within-call ordering is deterministic. Cross-call ordering in batch aggregation is non-deterministic but security-irrelevant since verification is local and outputs a boolean.

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation in c-kzg-4844 follows deterministic canonical order: domain separator (RCKZGCBATCH__V1_), FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL (uint64), num_commitments (uint64), num_cells (uint64), unique commitments (deduplication-order), then per-cell: commitment_indices[i] (uint64), cell_indices[i] (uint64), cells[i] (BYTES_PER_CELL), proofs_bytes[i] (BYTES_PER_PROOF). This matches the Ethereum spec. Integer encoding uses little-endian consistently (bytes_from_uint64). The Go wrapper passes parameters in deterministic blob-index order within each sidecar.
state_anomalies_found: When batching multiple P2P requests in verifyKzgBatch, allDataColumns ordering depends on kzgChan arrival order — non-deterministic across nodes but not security-critical since verification is local
Deduplication order changes with input order — different orderings produce different Fiat-Shamir challenge r, but verification result (pass/fail) is unaffected for correct data
phase1_abstract_interpretation.cache_analysis: No ordering-sensitive caching in the verification path
phase1_abstract_interpretation.concurrency_analysis: Go map iteration is randomized but maps are not used in the critical verification path

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample found for ordering-based attack. Different Fiat-Shamir challenge r values (due to ordering differences) cannot make invalid cells pass verification, because r is used only for linear combination aggregation. Invalid data fails with overwhelming probability (1 - 1/p) for any random r, regardless of ordering.
phase2_symbolic_execution.counterexample: None — r affects aggregation efficiency but not soundness; invalid data fails for any r ≠ 0
attack_scenarios: Ordering manipulation cannot cause invalid data to pass KZG verification
phase2_symbolic_execution.timing_dependencies: None — ordering is irrelevant to security

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Hash ordering is determined locally by each node's processing order. Since each node runs verification independently and the output is boolean (valid/invalid) — not a consensus-critical value that all nodes must agree on — ordering differences cannot cause consensus divergence.
entry_points: P2P gossip (ordering depends on receipt time)
phase2_5_reachability_analysis.attack_surface: No external attack surface — ordering is locally determined and security-irrelevant for boolean output

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The invariant 'hash input order is deterministic and consistent' holds within a single call to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. The c-kzg-4844 implementation matches the Ethereum spec ordering within a single call. Cross-node ordering differences are not a consensus concern because verification is local.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Canonical ordering enforced by c-kzg-4844 C library within each verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch invocation
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient — ordering within a single call is deterministic and spec-compliant. Cross-call ordering is security-irrelevant.
edge_cases: If the Ethereum spec evolves to require cross-node consistency of KZG challenge values (e.g., for proof aggregation), this would need revisiting — not applicable in current Fulu spec

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No vulnerability. The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation is deterministic within a single library call per spec. The c-kzg-4844 library ordering matches the Ethereum Fulu spec exactly. Cross-implementation ordering differences in batch aggregation are not a security concern because verification is local and outputs a boolean result.
phase3_5_scope_filtering.recommendation: Document that batch ordering is internally consistent per the c-kzg-4844 spec but need not be consistent across separate calls or nodes, as verification is a local operation.

audit_items.reasoning: The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation is deterministic and spec-compliant within each verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch call. The c-kzg-4844 C library enforces canonical ordering matching the Ethereum Fulu spec (domain separator, constants, unique commitments, per-cell data). Cross-implementation ordering of batch aggregation is not a security concern because each node independently verifies and outputs a boolean result — not a consensus-critical value requiring cross-node agreement.
